extracted.intended_audience: advanced TeX users, macro/font designers, and implementers of TeX math typesetting
extracted.subtask_description: Detailed specifications and parameterized rules from The TeXbook for converting math lists into horizontal lists (generating boxes), symbol/delimiter handling, punctuation spacing, and hyphenation algorithm behavior. Intended to guide font designers and macro writers implementing or customizing TeX math layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negated relations (use of \not and special sequences)
rubrics_metrics.description:
Many relation symbols can be negated by prefixing with 
ot; 
ot is a relation character of width zero so it overlaps the following relation. Because positioning may be suboptimal for some relations (e.g., 
ot\in produces a shallow slash), TeX provides special control sequences for preferred glyphs (e.g., 
otin).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer special negated-relation control sequences like \notin when available because \not is zero-width and may produce poor cancellation positioning; Appendix B shows how to define similar symbols.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrows and placing material over relations (\buildrel)
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX provides many arrow relation symbols (uparrow, Uparrow, downarrow, Leftarrow, longrightarrow, etc.). To place symbols over arrows/relations, use \buildrel <superscript> \over <relation>, which places the superscript above the relation as limits are placed over large operators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: to label a long arrow with \alpha\beta you would write \buildrel \alpha\beta \over \longrightarrow. Note: in this context \over does not create a fraction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Left delimiters (openings) and scalable delimiters
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX supplies left delimiters besides '(' such as \lbrack, \lbrace, \lfloor, \langle, \lceil and these grow when prefixed by \bigl, \Bigl, \biggl, \Biggl or by \left. Additional combinations (e.g., \lbrack\!\lbrack, \langle\!\langle, (\!( ) ) ) are available at text size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use \left/\right and the \big* family to get properly sized delimiters. Chapter 17 mentions \lgroup and \lmoustache for larger sizes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right delimiters (closings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Corresponding right delimiters are available (\rbrack, \rbrace, \rfloor, \rangle, \rceil) and behave analogously to left delimiters but reversed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Everything that works for openings works also for closings; apply the same sizing tricks in reverse.

rubrics_metrics.name: Punctuation spacing in math (commas, semicolons, colon)
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX inserts a thin space after commas and semicolons in math formulas; for a colon to get this spacing you should use \colon (otherwise colon is treated as a relation). Plain TeX also defines \ldotp and \cdotp ('.' and '·' with comma/semicolon spacing) used in definitions of \ldots and \cdots.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: use $f\colon A\rightarrow B$ not $f:A\rightarrow B$ if you want colon spacing; $L(a,b;c\colon x,y;z)$ shows combined use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternate control-sequence names and aliasing
rubrics_metrics.description:
If you prefer another name for a math symbol you can alias it (e.g., \let\cupcap=\asymp). Plain TeX also defines many alternate names for common symbols (e.g., 
e and 
eq both mean 
ot=; \le and \leq are equivalent, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may create aliases for readability and mnemonic convenience. Plain TeX already provides many common equivalents (list includes ne/neq, le/<=, ge/>=, to/gets, land/lor, lnot/neg, vert/|, etc.). Note: \iff behaves like \Longleftrightarrow but adds extra thick space at each side.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-math symbols available outside math mode
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX exposes § (\S), ¶ (\P), dagger (\dag), and double dagger (\ddag) as special symbols typeset from the math font but intended for text mode; \dagger and \ddagger exist for math mode.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These control sequences do not change size in subscripts/superscripts; when using them in math you must write $x^{\P}$ rather than $x^\P$. You can define mathematical equivalents if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of Appendix G (precise positioning rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explains the precise positioning rules by which TeX converts a math list into a horizontal list; intended for people who define new math fonts and/or macros and need to know exactly how TeX manipulates formula constituents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advises that readers should review Chapter 17 introduction to math lists first; many subtle interactions depend on the starting style and many font parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Font parameter requirements for symbol and extension fonts
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX requires \textfont2, \scriptfont2, \scriptscriptfont2 each contain at least 22 \fontdimen parameters (denoted σ1..σ22), and the three fonts in family 3 must each have at least 13 \fontdimen parameters (denoted ξ1..ξ13).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These parameters control many aspects of math layout; when creating fonts supply the required parameters or TeX cannot typeset formulas correctly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting style, style ordering, and style-derived superscript/subscript styles
rubrics_metrics.description: A math list is typeset in a starting style C (e.g., displayed formulas use D, text equations use T). The eight styles order is D > D0 > T > T0 > S > S0 > SS > SS0; C↑ denotes the superscript style for C and C↓ its subscript style. Penalties may or may not be inserted depending on whether formulas are in paragraphs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many rules use comparisons like C ≤ S to choose behavior; be careful to derive C↑, C↓ and to know whether penalties are active (paragraph vs display).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subroutine: set box x to the specified field in a given style
rubrics_metrics.description: When setting box x to a field: (a) empty field → null box; (b) field with a symbol → hbox containing symbol in appropriate size including italic correction in width; (c) field containing a math or horizontal list → hbox containing the result of typesetting that list with the specified starting style. Glue is set with no stretch/shrink and redundant hboxing is omitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subroutine is repeatedly referenced by later rules for assembling nuclei, subscripts, superscripts, accents, radicals, fractions, etc.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subroutine: set box x to a variable delimiter (search algorithm)
rubrics_metrics.description: A variable delimiter is defined by small character a (family f) and large character b (family g). Search order: look at a in scriptscriptfont f if C ≤ SS, then scriptfont f if C ≤ S, then textfont f; if unsuitable, try b in the same order. If none suitable, choose the character with greatest height+depth; if none exist set x to empty box of width \nulldelimiterspace. If extensible character found, build vbox from pieces; otherwise set x to hbox of found character including italic correction in width.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a character has a successor in the font, the successor is examined next. Extensible characters are built from repeatable pieces; width and height rules for the resulting box are specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subroutine: rebox a given box to a given width
rubrics_metrics.description: To rebox: if width differs, unpackage (unless vbox), add kern for italic correction if implied, insert \hss glue at both left and right, and package into an hbox. Used to give common width to numerator/denominator and center the smaller unless infinite glue is present.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This centers content horizontally by adding flexible glue; used frequently in fraction and limit constructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviations for box dimensions (h(x), d(x), w(x))
rubrics_metrics.description: If x is a box, h(x), d(x), and w(x) denote its height, depth, and width respectively.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These abbreviations are used throughout the rules to compute placements and clearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 1: leave special items unchanged
rubrics_metrics.description: If current math item is a rule or discretionary or penalty or 'whatsit' or boundary item, leave it unchanged and move to next item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items do not need translation during the first pass.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 2: glue and kern translation (mu conversion and \nonscript handling)
rubrics_metrics.description: If current item is glue or a kern: if glue from \nonscript check the next item and if it is glue or kern remove it when C ≤ S. If glue is from \mskip or \mkern, convert mu to absolute units by multiplying each finite dimension by 1/18 σ6. Then proceed to next item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Accurate mu conversion depends on σ6; \nonscript glue is conditional on style > S and should be pruned appropriately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3: style change items
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a style change, set C to the specified style, delete the item from the list, and continue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Style items affect subsequent processing and must be removed during the first pass after updating the current style.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 4: four-way choice items
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a four-way choice (contains four math lists for the main styles), replace it by the list corresponding to current style C and continue at the first unprocessed item.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These represent style-dependent alternatives and are resolved immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 5: Bin atom handling (contextual conversion to Ord)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a Bin atom and it is the first atom in the list or the most recent previous atom was Bin, Op, Rel, Open, or Punct, change the current Bin to Ord and continue with Rule 14; otherwise continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enforces proper spacing and prevents binary operators from appearing where they should be ordinary symbols (e.g., at the start of expression).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 6: Rel/Close/Punct following Bin conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: If the current item is a Rel or Close or Punct atom and the most recent previous atom was Bin, change that previous Bin to Ord. Continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures Bin atoms are not left in contexts that would create incorrect spacing before relations, closers, or punctuation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 7: Open or Inner atoms go to Rule 17
rubrics_metrics.description: If current item is an Open or Inner atom, process it directly at Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opens/Inner atoms require only the remaining processing (e.g., attachment of scripts) handled later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 8: Vcenter (\vcenter) atom conversion
rubrics_metrics.description: If item is a Vcent atom, let its nucleus be a vbox of height-plus-depth v. Change the height to (1/2)2 v − a and the depth to (1/2)2 v + a where a is axis height σ22; change atom type to Ord and continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centers the vbox on the math axis; precise arithmetic given in the rule must be followed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 9: Over atom (\overline) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For Over atom, set box x to the nucleus in style C0. Replace nucleus by a vbox: kern θ, hrule of height θ, kern 3θ, box x (top to bottom), where θ = ξ8 (default rule thickness).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creates an overline with 3θ clearance and assumes θ units of white space above the rule; continue with Rule 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 10: Under atom (\underline) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For Under atom, set box x to nucleus in style C. Replace nucleus by vtop assembled from box x, kern 3θ, hrule of height θ (θ = ξ8) and add θ to the depth of the box (rule placed below nucleus).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Places an underline with the same spacing conventions as overlines; continue with Rule 16.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 11: Radical (\sqrt) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For Rad atom: set box x to nucleus in style C0. Let θ = ξ8 and ϕ = σ5 if C > T else ϕ = θ. Set ψ = θ + 1/4 |ϕ| (minimum clearance between box x and rule). Set box y to a variable delimiter with height+depth ≥ h(x)+d(x)+ψ+θ then set θ ← h(y) (rule thickness). If d(y) is large, increase ψ appropriately. Construct vbox of kern θ, hrule θ, kern ψ, box x; replace nucleus by box y raised by h(x)+ψ followed by this vbox.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Matches radical glyph metrics to the content box and uses font-specified radical thickness; precise numeric adjustments must be followed for correct spacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 12: Math accents (\mathaccent) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: For Acc atom: if accent character doesn’t exist in the current size, skip to Rule 16. Otherwise set box x to nucleus in style C0, compute width u, compute skew s if nucleus is single character, possibly switch accent to successor if font successor fits, compute δ = min(h(x), x-height of accent font). For single-character nuclei, combine nucleus and its scripts into box x and adjust δ. Put accent in box y including italic correction and build vbox z containing y shifted right by s + 1/2(u − w(y)), kern −δ, and box x, adjusting heights and widths as necessary; replace nucleus by z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful handling of successors, italic corrections, skewchar and x-height ensures accents are positioned correctly; follow the step-by-step construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 13/13a: Operators and limits (\limits / \displaylimits)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Op atoms, mark limits if \limits or if \displaylimits and C > T. If nucleus is a symbol, promote to successor in display styles if available, put symbol into box x and set δ to italic correction (included in width only if limits or no subscript). Center operator vertically on axis (shift by 1/2(h(x) − d(x)) − a where a = σ22). If limits are to be typeset, set boxes for superscript/subscript in appropriate sizes, rebox to max widths, attach superscript above with kern max(ξ9, ξ11 − d(x)) and shift right by 1/2 δ, and subscript below with kern max(ξ10, ξ12 − h(z)) and shift left by 1/2 δ; add ξ13 spacing above/below as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This defines when and how limits are positioned above/below large operators and how operator size succession is handled in display styles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 14: Ord atom text symbol detection, ligatures and kern insertion
rubrics_metrics.description: If current item is Ord, normally go to Rule 17 unless: nucleus is a symbol, both sub/superscripts empty, next item is an atom of type Ord/Op/Bin/Rel/Open/Close/Punct whose nucleus is a symbol of same family. Then mark current as a text symbol; if font info shows a ligature between the symbols insert the ligature character; if font info shows a kern insert a kern item. After processing ligatures/kerns, continue to Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This handles inter-letter ligatures and font-specified kerning between adjacent text symbols in math mode.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 15/15a-e: Generalized fractions and delimiter handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Generalized fraction handling: let θ be bar thickness (ξ8 for \over, 0 for \atop, given value for \above). Put numerator box x and denominator box z using appropriate styles (T/T0 or C↑/C↓), rebox to equal widths, select u and v vertical shifts based on style and θ, ensure minimum clearances ϕ and adjust u/v accordingly for \atop (θ=0) or \over (θ≠0). Construct vbox with numerator, optional hrule and denominator positioned so hrule middle placed at axis a = σ22 − 1/2 θ. Enclose with delimiters whose height+depth ≥ σ20 if C > T else ≥ σ21 and center them; replace fraction by Inner atom with sequence (left delimiter, vbox, right delimiter).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed numeric formulas govern vertical shifts, minimum clearances, and delimiter sizing; follow 15a–15e to implement fractions precisely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 16: Convert current item to Ord and continue
rubrics_metrics.description: Change the current item to an Ord atom and continue with Rule 17.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used after certain transformations (e.g., Over/Under handled) to normalize atom type before final processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 17: Translating nucleus symbols to character boxes
rubrics_metrics.description: If nucleus is a math list, replace it by a box typeset in current style. If nucleus is a symbol, convert to a character box for the specified family/size; set δ to italic correction unless the symbol was marked as text symbol or the font's \fontdimen2 is zero. If δ nonzero and subscript empty, insert kern of width δ after the char box and set δ to zero. Continue with Rule 18.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This produces the base glyph box and possibly inserts italic correction kern which affects subsequent script placement and horizontal displacement δ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 18 (and subrules a–f): Attaching subscripts and superscripts
rubrics_metrics.description: If no sub/superscripts, continue. Otherwise: 18a compute preliminary u and v shift minima (if nucleus is a char box set u=v=0 else u=h−q, v=d+r with q,r from σ18,σ19); 18b if superscript empty (only subscript) set box x to subscript in style C↓ add \scriptspace to width and append shifted down by max(v, σ16, h(x)−4/5|σ5|); 18c set box x to superscript in style C↑ add \scriptspace; set u=max(u, p, d(x)+1/4|σ5|) where p depends on C; 18d if subscript empty append superscript shifted up by u; else set box y to subscript style C↓ add \scriptspace and v=max(v, σ17); 18e ensure clearance between subscript and superscript at least 4ξ8, otherwise adjust v; also ensure superscript baseline at least 4/5 x-height by adjusting u/v; 18f assemble vbox of height h(x)+u and depth d(y)+v with horizontal displacement δ (from earlier rules) and append.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A detailed sequence of numeric constraints ensures scripts don't collide and meet typographic minima; many σ and ξ parameters are used to compute shifts and clearances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 19: Boundary item handling and delimiter sizing for entire formula
rubrics_metrics.description: If math list begins and ends with boundary items, compute maximum height h and depth d of boxes from first pass (considering raises/lowers). Let a = σ22 axis height and δ = max(h − a, d + a). Replace boundaries by delimiters whose height+depth ≥ max(bδ/500c f, 2δ − l) where f=\delimiterfactor and l=\delimitershortfall; shift delimiters to vertical center relative to axis. Change left boundary to Open atom and right to Close atom. (Calculations use the starting style C.)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This chooses suitably large delimiters for whole-formula boundaries, using integer/dimension parameters that depend on font metrics and global delimiter parameters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 20: Second pass — atom replacement and inter-element spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: After Rules 1–19 convert math list so only atom types Ord, Op, Bin, Rel, Open, Close, Punct, Inner remain. Second pass replaces atoms by their boxes and kerns and inserts inter-element spacing before each atom except the first, based on the atom types using \thinmuskip, \medmuskip, and \thickmuskip (mu units converted as in Rule 2). Style items are removed but their style effects apply consistently between passes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inter-element spacing rules from Chapter 18 define the spacing matrix; some of these mu glues are \nonscript and thus only inserted in styles > S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 21: Penalties after Bin and Rel atoms in paragraph formulas
rubrics_metrics.description: When math list is part of a paragraph, place penalties after each Bin and Rel: \binoppenalty after Bin and \relpenalty after Rel. Exceptions: no penalty after final item, or if existing penalty value ≥ 10000, or if next item is already a penalty, or after a Rel immediately followed by another Rel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These penalties help TeX line-breaking; follow exceptions to avoid redundant or blocking penalties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 22: Final conversion and enclosing by math-on/math-off
rubrics_metrics.description: After all transformations the math list is a horizontal list. If inserted into a larger horizontal list, enclose it by 'math-on' and 'math-off' items that record current \mathsurround. If the list is a displayed formula, it is further processed as explained in Chapter 19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect \mathsurround when embedding inline formulas; displayed formulas follow additional display-mode layout rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of parameter usage (σ and ξ mappings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Index mapping which font/TeX parameters affect which rules: σ5 = x-height, σ6 = quad, σ8..σ13 sup/sub parameters, σ14..σ19 sup/sub drop, σ20/σ21 delim1/delim2, σ22 axis height; ξ8 default rule thickness; ξ9..ξ13 big-op spacing parameters. The table indicates which rules use which parameters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful study of the mapping helps font designers set parameters to achieve desired vertical/horizontal metrics; external names like 'sup2' for σ14 and 'default rule thickness' for ξ8 are commonly used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation: use of exception dictionary before pattern matching
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX hyphenates a word by first looking in an 'exception dictionary' that specifies hyphen positions for special-case words; if not found it applies pattern matching (Liang’s algorithm).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a word needs forced or special hyphenation (e.g., differing noun/verb hyphenation) add it to the exception dictionary to override pattern behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Liang's pattern algorithm (pattern dictionary, subwords and interletter values)
rubrics_metrics.description: Liang’s method extends the word with markers at ends and considers subwords of various lengths. Each pattern defines k+1 interletter integer values; TeX computes the maximum interletter value at each position from matching patterns. A hyphen is allowed at positions whose resulting interletter value is odd.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patterns are designed so odd values indicate acceptable breakpoints while even values suppress breaks; algorithm is language-adaptable and works efficiently with compact pattern tables.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern / example behavior (how odd/even values produce hyphens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Example: for 'hyphenation' patterns yield .0h0y3p0h0e2n5a4t2i0o2n0 and odd interletter values indicate breaks producing 'hy-phen-ation'. For 'concatenation' patterns yield breaks at odd positions 'con-cate-na-tion'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examples illustrate how pattern subscripts combine and how maxima determine final interletter scores; odd → break, even → no break.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pattern table coverage and refinement procedure (Liang's corpus work)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plain TeX loads 4447 patterns derived by Liang from a specially prepared dictionary plus checks against a larger hyphenation dictionary; a few thousand common words were weighted and about 1000 exceptions were added to the pocket dictionary to tune errors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The result finds 89.3% of hyphens in the original dictionary and inserts no hyphens not present there; common and technical words are specially favored to guarantee correct hyphenation of frequent terms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation behavior on foreign/long/exceptional words
rubrics_metrics.description: Liang patterns generalize reasonably to unfamiliar words and foreign names not far from English; they perform well on long coined words (example: 'supercalifragilisticexpialidocious') and somewhat tolerably on other-language constructs, but pure linguistic differences (e.g., Welsh place names) expose pattern limitations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When precise hyphenation is required for unusual foreign words, add word to exception dictionary or supply language-specific patterns; expect degraded results for languages with very different syllabification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hyphenation tuning parameters and penalties
rubrics_metrics.description: TeX exposes parameters affecting hyphenation/line breaking such as \hyphenpenalty, \pretolerance, \tolerance, \doublehyphendemerits, \finalhyphendemerits which interact with hyphenation decisions and line-breaking quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adjust these global parameters to change how readily TeX hyphenates and to balance hyphenation against other line-breaking costs.
